# Spinal Cord Stimulator Clinical Compass

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | RVU | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 63650 | Percutaneous implantation of neurostimulator electrode array, epidural | 14.22 | SCS trial electrode placement — percutaneous |
| 63655 | Laminectomy for implantation of neurostimulator electrodes, plate/paddle, epidural | 22.44 | SCS trial — surgical paddle electrode |
| 63685 | Insertion or replacement of spinal neurostimulator pulse generator or receiver, direct or inductive coupling | 8.92 | Permanent IPG implantation |
| 63688 | Revision or removal of implanted spinal neurostimulator electrode array | 10.12 | Electrode revision or removal |
| 63663 | Revision including replacement, when performed, of spinal neurostimulator electrode percutaneous array(s), including fluoroscopy, when performed | 9.44 | Percutaneous electrode revision |
| 95970 | Electronic analysis of implanted neurostimulator pulse generator/transmitter | 0.62 | Programming — initial |
| 95971 | Electronic analysis of implanted neurostimulator pulse generator/transmitter; with simple programming | 0.92 | Programming — simple |

## ICD-10 Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G89.29 | Other chronic pain | Chronic pain — primary indication |
| G89.21 | Chronic pain due to trauma | Post-traumatic chronic pain |
| M54.4 | Lumbago with sciatica | Failed back surgery syndrome with radiculopathy |
| M96.1 | Postlaminectomy syndrome, not elsewhere classified | Failed back surgery syndrome (FBSS) |
| G57.10 | Meralgia paresthetica, unspecified lower limb | Peripheral neuropathy |
| I73.9 | Peripheral vascular disease, unspecified | Critical limb ischemia indication |
| G54.2 | Cervical root disorders, not elsewhere classified | Cervical radiculopathy |
| G89.28 | Other chronic postprocedural pain | Post-surgical chronic pain |

## Payer Requirements

Tabs: Medicare | Medicaid | Private Insurance

### Medicare

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Diagnosis of chronic intractable pain of neuropathic origin (≥6 months duration)
- Failed conservative therapy: ≥6 months PT, medications (opioids, anticonvulsants, antidepressants)
- Psychological evaluation clearing patient for implant (no untreated psychiatric contraindications)
- No active substance use disorder or drug-seeking behavior
- No surgical contraindications (coagulopathy, active infection, cardiac pacemaker incompatibility)
- Trial stimulation (≥50% pain relief) required before permanent implant
- Multidisciplinary pain evaluation documentation

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Chronic neuropathic pain ≥6 months (FBSS, CRPS, peripheral neuropathy, radiculopathy)
- Failed conservative therapy including medications and PT
- Positive psychological evaluation
- Successful trial stimulation (≥50% pain relief)

**Reimbursement:** Medicare covers SCS under NCD 160.7. Trial (63650) and permanent implant (63685) are separately covered. Device costs are included in the facility fee. Psychological evaluation is a required prerequisite.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicare (CMS) | Covered per NCD 160.7; psychological eval required; ≥50% trial relief required for permanent implant | Yes |

### Medicaid

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- State-specific prior authorization required
- Chronic intractable pain documentation
- Failed conservative therapy documentation
- Psychological evaluation
- Trial stimulation results

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Chronic neuropathic pain with failed conservative therapy
- Positive psychological evaluation
- Successful trial stimulation

**Reimbursement:** Medicaid coverage varies significantly by state. Many states require prior authorization and follow Medicare NCD criteria. Some states have additional restrictions.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicaid (state-specific) | Coverage varies; most states follow Medicare NCD 160.7 criteria | Yes |

### Private Insurance

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Prior authorization required by all commercial payers
- Chronic intractable pain ≥6 months with neuropathic etiology
- Failed conservative therapy: ≥6 months PT, medications (≥2 drug classes), interventional procedures
- Psychological evaluation clearing patient for implant
- No active substance use disorder
- Trial stimulation results (≥50% pain relief required for permanent implant)
- Multidisciplinary pain program evaluation
- Peer-to-peer review typically required

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Chronic neuropathic pain ≥6 months (FBSS, CRPS, peripheral neuropathy)
- Failed conservative therapy including medications and PT
- Positive psychological evaluation
- Successful trial stimulation (≥50% relief)

**Reimbursement:** Commercial payers typically cover SCS with prior authorization and positive trial. Device costs may be subject to separate authorization. High denial rates — peer-to-peer review is almost always required.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aetna | Covered; requires psychological eval, 6-month conservative therapy failure, and ≥50% trial relief | Yes |
| UnitedHealthcare | Covered with prior auth; multidisciplinary evaluation and trial required | Yes |
| BCBS (most plans) | Covered; psychological eval and positive trial required; peer-to-peer often needed | Yes |
| Cigna | Covered with prior auth; strict criteria — psychological eval and trial mandatory | Yes |
| Humana | Covered; prior auth required; psychological eval and trial documentation mandatory | Yes |

## Required Documentation

### Pain History
- H&P documenting chronic pain diagnosis, duration (≥6 months), and neuropathic etiology
- Pain scores at multiple visits (NRS or VAS)
- Functional impairment documentation (ODI, PDI, or similar)
- Prior surgical history (for FBSS patients)

### Failed Conservative Therapy
- PT notes documenting ≥6 months of comprehensive pain rehabilitation
- Medication trial documentation (opioids, anticonvulsants, antidepressants — ≥2 drug classes)
- Prior interventional procedure documentation (ESI, facet injections, etc.)
- Documentation of inadequate response or intolerance to each treatment

### Psychological Evaluation
- Formal psychological evaluation by licensed psychologist or psychiatrist
- Clearance for implant (no untreated psychiatric contraindications)
- Absence of active substance use disorder
- Coping skills and support system assessment

### Trial Documentation
- Trial procedure note (63650) with electrode placement confirmation
- Pain diary during trial period (minimum 3–7 days)
- ≥50% pain relief documented during trial
- Functional improvement during trial
- Patient satisfaction with trial stimulation

### Medical Clearance
- Absence of coagulopathy or anticoagulation contraindication
- Absence of active infection
- Cardiac device compatibility check (if pacemaker/ICD present)
- Surgical clearance if comorbidities present

## Submission Process

1. Establish chronic neuropathic pain diagnosis with ≥6 months duration documentation
2. Document failed conservative therapy (≥6 months PT, ≥2 medication classes, prior interventions)
3. Obtain psychological evaluation clearing patient for implant
4. Submit prior authorization for trial (63650) with full clinical documentation
5. Perform trial stimulation and document ≥50% pain relief in pain diary
6. Submit prior authorization for permanent implant (63685) with trial results
7. Include all documentation: pain history, failed therapy, psychological eval, trial diary
8. Request peer-to-peer review — almost always required for commercial payers
9. For device authorization: submit separately if payer requires device-specific approval

## Common Denial Reasons

- ⚠ Insufficient conservative therapy documentation — most common denial; document ≥6 months PT and ≥2 medication classes explicitly
- ⚠ Missing psychological evaluation — required by all payers; must be from licensed psychologist/psychiatrist
- ⚠ Trial relief <50% — document pain diary with specific % relief at each time point
- ⚠ Active substance use disorder not addressed — document substance use evaluation and treatment
- ⚠ Diagnosis not meeting neuropathic criteria — specify FBSS, CRPS, peripheral neuropathy, or radiculopathy
- ⚠ Missing peer-to-peer review — proactively request for all commercial payer submissions
- ⚠ Device authorization not separately obtained — verify if payer requires separate device approval
- ⚠ Prior authorization not obtained before trial procedure
